description: Represent integer vectors whose length may be large but whose nonzero entries are few, then compute their dot product. Example 1: [1,0,0,2,3] dotted with [0,3,0,4,0] is 8. Example 2: [-1,0,0,0,0] dotted with [0,0,0,0,2] is 0. Constraints: both vectors have equal length, and most entries may be zero.
intuition: Only positions nonzero in both vectors can contribute to the sum.

brute_force.approach: Store both full vectors and multiply corresponding entries across the entire length.

optimal.approach: Store only nonzero index-value pairs and iterate the smaller sparse map while looking up matching indices in the other.

edge_cases: A vector with no nonzero values always yields a zero dot product.
Negative values contribute with their signed product.
